title: Ecommerce payment gateway: A guide for Singapore sellers
summary: How Singapore online stores choose an ecommerce payment gateway: PayNow and cards, fees, cross-border selling, and the best options in 2026.
body_markdown:
## What is an ecommerce payment gateway


An ecommerce payment gateway is what takes the money at your online checkout. A shopper taps pay. The gateway locks their card or wallet details, sends them off for approval, and comes back with a yes or a no, usually before they've looked up from their phone. When it works, nobody notices it. That is the point.


These two terms are often confused:


- The gateway is the checkout end. It collects the payment and keeps the data secure.


- The[processor](http://aspireapp.com/blog/best-ecommerce-payment-processing-solutions) is the back office. It moves the money between the banks.


Most providers today do both jobs, so you rarely shop for them separately. If you want the full mechanics and the gateway-versus-processor detail, we've covered that in[payment gateways: features, benefits, and how to choose](https://aspireapp.com/blog/payment-gateways-features-benefits-how-to-choose) . This guide stays on the part that matters for an online store in Singapore.


## How a payment gateway works on your ecommerce website


You don't need the engineering view, just the shape of it. From the moment someone pays, a payment gateway for ecommerce website checkout runs through roughly five steps:


- The shopper picks a method at checkout, a card, PayNow, or a wallet, and confirms.


- The gateway encrypts those details so your own servers never hold raw card numbers.


- It sends the request to the bank or payment method to approve or decline.


- The answer comes back, and your store shows "paid" or asks them to try again.


- The funds settle into your account on the provider's schedule, often a day or two later.


The gap between step four and step five is the one people forget. A sale can read as successful long before the cash is usable. That timing is part of why an e-commerce payment gateway is a cash-flow decision, not only a checkout one.


## What Singapore shoppers expect at checkout


Local payment preferences can help your store create a smoother checkout and convert more shoppers. In Singapore, offering the methods customers already know and trust can make it easier to grow your sales.


A payment gateway in ecommerce website checkouts should, at a minimum, cover what people in Singapore actually reach for:


- **PayNow.** Fast, familiar, and cheap to accept. For a lot of local buyers, it's the default now, especially on mobile.


- **Cards.** Visa and Mastercard are non-negotiable. Amex if your margins allow it.


- [Digital wallets](http://aspireapp.com/blog/different-payment-methods-for-your-e-commerce-business) **.** GrabPay, Apple Pay, and Google Pay cover most of the rest.


- **Buy Now, Pay Later.** Atome and GrabPay PayLater help on higher-value carts, where people hesitate.


You don't have to offer everything on day one. But your ecommerce payment gateway is where these expectations either get met or quietly cost you, so if PayNow is missing and your buyers are mostly local, you're leaving money on the table without seeing it happen.


## What to look for in an ecommerce payment gateway


Beyond the headline rate, a handful of things decide whether an ecommerce payment gateway fits your store. The strongest payment gateway solutions for ecommerce business owners tend to share the same short list, and it's worth checking before you commit, because switching later is a nuisance.


### Local payment method coverage


Confirm your ecommerce payment gateway supports PayNow and the wallets your customers use, not just cards. Coverage varies more than the marketing suggests, so check the Singapore page, not the global one.


### Fees, and the fees behind the fees


The card rate is the number everyone quotes. It's rarely the whole cost. Watch for:


- Cross-border or international card surcharges, which vary by provider and can add to the standard card processing fee.


- Currency conversion fees when a sale isn't in SGD.


- Chargeback and refund charges.


- Any monthly or platform-plugin fee.


An ecommerce payment gateway with a low card rate can still be an expensive option once your order mix includes overseas cards.


### Ecommerce platform integration


If you're on Shopify or WooCommerce, check whether the gateway has a reliable, maintained integration for your platform. A ready-made integration can make setup much simpler, while an API-only option may require more development work. Check this before anything else, because it can rule a provider out on its own.


### Settlement speed


[Faster payouts mean healthier cash flow](http://aspireapp.com/blog/understanding-burn-rate) . Some providers settle the next day, others take several days. If you restock often or run tight on working capital, this matters more than a fractional difference in fees.


### Multi-currency and cross-border payments


If you sell overseas, look beyond the domestic payment experience. Check whether the gateway allows you to hold or settle funds in the currencies you sell in, what FX margin applies when you convert, and whether it supports local payment methods in your key markets.


For a Singapore store expanding internationally, these costs can have a bigger impact on margins than a small difference in the domestic card rate. Before committing, consider running a small live test of the provider's onboarding, checkout and settlement process.


## Security and MAS licensing


Security and compliance matter just as much as payment methods and pricing. A good ecommerce payment gateway should help protect transactions from fraud while keeping payment data secure and meeting the regulatory requirements that apply in Singapore.


- **Fraud screening and risk scoring:** Automated checks can assess transactions for unusual behaviour and flag potentially fraudulent payments.


- **3D Secure 2:** Adds an extra layer of cardholder authentication for eligible transactions and can help reduce unauthorised card payments.


- **Velocity rules:** Lets you set limits on how often transactions can be attempted within a given period, helping flag unusual activity such as repeated payment attempts.


- **Tokenisation:** Replaces sensitive card details with tokens, reducing the need to expose or store the underlying card number.


- **CVV and address checks:** Where supported and applicable, these can provide additional signals when assessing card transactions.


- **Chargeback and dispute management:** Look for tools that help you receive alerts, respond to disputes and keep track of chargebacks.


- **False-decline controls:** Good fraud controls should block suspicious transactions without unnecessarily rejecting genuine customers.


- **Transaction monitoring:** Ongoing monitoring can help identify unusual patterns after a payment has been approved.


PCI DSS is another important benchmark. It sets baseline security requirements for businesses that store, process or transmit payment card data.


For Singapore businesses, also check the provider's regulatory status with the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS). The MAS Financial Institutions Directory shows the licences and regulated payment services held by financial institutions, so you can verify the provider rather than relying only on its website claims.


## Best payment gateways for ecommerce in Singapore


There's no single best payment gateway for ecommerce, only the one that fits how you sell. The payment gateway ecommerce stores in Singapore lean on usually comes down to the shortlist below. Here's how the main options compare before the short profiles.


\[Table:1\]


- **Stripe:** Strong if you have a developer or want control over the checkout. Deep documentation, good local method coverage, and native Shopify and WooCommerce support. Costs climb on cross-border orders, so read the FX terms.


- **Airwallex:** Built for stores that sell beyond Singapore. It lets you settle like-for-like in multiple currencies and hold funds, so you're not force-converting every sale. Plugins for the main platforms plus a hosted checkout.


- **HitPay:** The most local-first of the group, with the broadest PayNow and wallet coverage and the lowest headline card rate. The catch is a small extra fee when you run it through a platform plugin, which narrows the gap.


- **Adyen:** Enterprise-grade, and priced and built for that. Interchange++ pricing is transparent at volume but hard to forecast for a smaller store, and setup needs technical work.


- **PayPal:** Worth having as a secondary option for overseas buyers who trust the brand. As a primary gateway, it tends to cost more and pulls customers off your site to pay.


## Selling across borders: the global gateway angle


This is where a lot of Singapore stores quietly lose margin, and where the best global payment gateway for ecommerce question really gets decided.


When an overseas customer pays you in USD, most gateways convert it straight to SGD and charge a spread to do it. Do that on every international order, and it adds up fast. The alternative is a provider that offers like-for-like settlement, meaning you receive USD as USD and convert on your own terms, or not at all if you have USD costs to cover.


If cross-border is a real part of your sales, a global-minded ecommerce payment gateway should let you weigh:


- Whether you can hold and settle in the currencies you actually sell in.


- The FX margin on conversion, not just the card rate.


- Whether local payment methods in your key markets are supported.


For a store selling across Southeast Asia or further, that FX handling often matters more to the bottom line than a fraction of a percent on the domestic card fee. It's usually what separates the best global payment gateway for ecommerce from one that's merely fine at home.


## Conclusion


The right payment gateway for ecommerce in Singapore isn't the cheapest sticker rate. The best ecommerce payment gateway for your store is the one that takes the payments your customers actually want to use, plugs into your platform without a project, and doesn't quietly erode your margin on cross-border sales. Get those three right and checkout stops being the place your hard-won traffic leaks away.

## Frequently asked questions


### What is the best payment gateway for ecommerce in Singapore?


There isn't one answer for every store. HitPay suits Singapore-focused sellers who want the deepest local method coverage, Stripe suits developer-led and global stores, and Airwallex suits businesses with heavy cross-border sales. Match it to your platform, your customers' preferred methods, and your order mix.


### Do I need a payment gateway for my ecommerce website?


Yes. Without an ecommerce payment gateway, you can't securely accept cards, wallets, or PayNow online. It's what encrypts payment details, gets the transaction approved, and moves funds to your account, so it's a requirement for any store taking online payments.


### How much does a payment gateway charge in Singapore?


Most charge roughly 2.8% to 4.4% per card transaction plus a small fixed fee. PayNow is cheaper, around 0.65% to 1.3%. International cards and currency conversion add more, so compare providers on your real transaction mix rather than the headline rate.


### Which payment gateways support PayNow and GrabPay?


HitPay, Airwallex, Stripe, and Adyen support PayNow, and most also support GrabPay, though coverage differs by provider. Confirm the exact local methods on the provider's Singapore page before you decide.


### What is the best global payment gateway for ecommerce?


For cross-border selling, look for like-for-like settlement and genuine multi-currency support, so you're not forcefully converting every overseas sale into SGD. An ecommerce payment gateway built for global commerce, such as Airwallex, tends to handle this better than one designed mainly for a single market.


### What are the types of payment gateways?


Payment gateways generally fall into four types, based on where the payment experience takes place and how the gateway connects to your ecommerce website:


- **Hosted or Redirect payment gateway:** The customer is taken to a separate payment page hosted by the payment provider to complete the transaction.


- **Self-hosted payment gateway:** The payment details are collected on your website, while the gateway handles the transaction processing in the background.


- **Integrated or API-hosted gateway:** The payment experience is built into your website through an API, giving you more control over the checkout experience.


- **Hybrid or Direct Post gateway:** The customer enters payment details on your website, but the information is sent directly to the payment provider for processing rather than being handled by your own server.
